title: Urgent-Care Addition to Emergency Supply Days after an Emergency Room Visit
content:
A Pharmacy Benefit member recently seen in the emergency room receives additional emergency supply days for a drug turned away at the counter for prior authorization.

**Rule.** The urgent-care addition is five days (5) where the member has a paid emergency-room emergency claim with a service date in the last month and the drug is an inhaler, one day (1) where the member has such a claim and the drug is not an inhaler, and nothing where the member has no such claim.

### Records read

- **Emergency-room claims** — claims booked on the member's Medicaid Managed Care Membership whose service category is emergency-room emergency and whose adjudication status is paid, with a service date in the last month.
- **The drug** — the drug named on the latest counter rejection for prior authorization on the member's pharmacy coverage; it is an inhaler when its drug name names an inhaler.

The addition is added to the request days in forming the counted emergency supply days, before the one-day floor applies to those counted days as a whole and before they are turned into dispensed days.

### Truth table

| Paid emergency-room emergency claim in the last month | Drug is an inhaler | Urgent-care addition |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 5 days |
| Yes | No | 1 day |
| No | Yes or No | Nothing |

### Cases (hypothetical)

- A paid emergency-room emergency claim three weeks ago; the drug is an albuterol inhaler: 5 days.
- The same claim; the drug is a tablet: 1 day.
- An emergency-room claim that was denied: not a paid claim, nothing.
